title: Risks of Human Spaceflight
section: Risk of Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
tags: fatigue sleep rest alertness concentration workload circadian schedule
passage: NASA identifies disrupted body clocks, recurring sleep loss, and sustained work demands as combined stressors that researchers study for their effects on crew health and safety.

title: Risks of Human Spaceflight
tags: chest heart cardiovascular palpitations blood pressure pulse resting
passage: Weightlessness changes circulation and how the heart and blood vessels work. NASA studies these adaptations and how to reduce their potential adverse effects.

title: Risks of Human Spaceflight
tags: bone musculoskeletal muscle gravity exercise joint strength
passage: Reduced loading in weightlessness can weaken bones. NASA studies how to quantify the changes and preserve bone strength through countermeasures.

title: 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight
tags: general wellness temperature abdomen mission radiation gravity distance confinement environment
passage: NASA groups the major hazards of exploration missions into radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity, and closed or hostile environments. These hazards can occur together.

title: Hazard: Isolation and Confinement
tags: brain concentration behavioral stress isolation mood
passage: NASA researchers are developing ways to monitor behavioral health and adapt tools for use in spaceflight so emerging concerns can be recognized earlier.

title: In-Flight Medical Reference Page
tags: emergency crew medical support communication procedure care
passage: In-flight care supports crew safety in an isolated setting where terrestrial medical treatment may be inaccessible. NASA provides a reference collection on medical operations and human spaceflight.
